findings.title: Persistent USE failure now drops every connection, taking a node's whole pool down
findings.claim: Previously a failed USE was logged but the connection still joined the pool; now every such connection is dropped and refilled with growing backoff and no exit, so a persistent USE failure (e.g. DROP KEYSPACE while use_keyspace is set) empties the pool, publishes Broken(UseKeyspaceError), and fires ConnectivityChangeEvent::Lost even for fully-qualified queries.

findings.title: Keyspace-failure logging dropped to debug and error only surfaces when pool is empty
findings.claim: The log level for the USE failure dropped from warn! to debug!, and the error is only published to shared_conns when the pool is empty and idle, so with one live connection a node that persistently rejects USE stays permanently under target with nothing visible at default log level, unlike the sibling use_keyspace path (line 1322) which still warns.

findings.title: Shard-aware connection rejection leaks +1 total_connections metric
findings.claim: When a shard-aware connection cannot be accepted, the Connection is dropped and replaced but the inc_total_connections counted at line 1051 is never reverted, leaking +1 per mismatched connection behind a port-rewriting NAT; pre-existing but contrary to the PR's stated goal of balancing metrics.

findings.title: PR's stated validation command never actually exercised the metrics test assertions
findings.claim: Since metrics is not a default feature, the validation command in the PR description compiled out every get_total_connections() assert and skipped the three #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] tests entirely; they do pass with --features metrics but the description should say so.

findings.title: PR description and commit messages omit most of the diff's substantive changes
findings.claim: Three of four commits (the metrics-balancing change) are not mentioned, and the reorder of keyspace setup ahead of maybe_reshard, the new public ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant, and the warn-to-debug change are all absent, with all four commit bodies empty despite the checklist claiming they explain the why.

findings.title: Moved keyspace-setup block lacks comment explaining why it must precede resharding
findings.claim: The comment is unchanged from main, so nothing stops a future refactor from moving the block back below the sharder update and reintroducing the bug that keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state guards against.

findings.title: ConnectionSetupError lacks #[derive(Debug)] and documentation of its invariant
findings.claim: Both payloads are Debug, so deriving it would let the test at 1668-1672 use .expect(); a doc line should state that Keyspace errors carry an already-counted connection and must never trigger the shard-aware port fallback.

findings.title: keyspace_name and result coupling in ConnectionSetupError is unenforced by the type
findings.claim: Err(Keyspace) with keyspace_name: None is impossible in production yet constructible, and the test at 1502-1506 builds exactly that; moving keyspace_name into the Ok payload would make it unrepresentable.

findings.title: #[from] publishes an unwanted impl From<UseKeyspaceError> for ConnectionError
findings.claim: UseKeyspaceError is also Session::use_keyspace's return type where it does not mean "connection unusable"; only one in-crate use exists (line 908), so the variant should be constructed explicitly instead of via #[from].

findings.title: Decrement loop should be a single atomic subtraction instead of looping
findings.claim: A dec_total_connections_by(n) should be added to both metrics backends and the loop dropped.

findings.title: Three duplicated "decrement + clear" sites for excess_connections should be one method
findings.claim: The decrement-and-clear logic is repeated at lines 674, 1031, and 1114 and should be folded into one clear_excess_connections() method.

findings.title: Decrement sites at each clear point lack comments explaining why they're safe
findings.claim: A maintainer needs to know these connections never reach remove_connection, otherwise the decrement at lines 674, 901, 1031, and 1114 looks like a double count.

findings.title: Two new test assertions are trivially true and don't prove a refill is scheduled
findings.claim: is_empty() and need_filling() hold on a fresh refiller before the event is handled, so they don't demonstrate a refill was actually scheduled; the meaningful assert at 1510 deserves a comment instead.

findings.title: No test drives the keyspace-failure backoff path through the actual run() loop
findings.claim: The backoff branch at 725-729 is only covered transitively; the full_pool_... test shows the spawn pattern that could be reused to cover it directly.

findings.title: Reshard-with-excess-connections term is never exercised by a test
findings.claim: excess_connections is empty at reshard time in the existing tests, so the + excess_connections.len() term at lines 1113-1115 never executes.

findings.title: New tests swallow proxy errors via let _ = proxy.finish().await
findings.claim: At lines 1939, 1967, and 2012 the tests discard the result of proxy.finish().await, hiding rule or frame failures, even though the same PR already uses the correct error-checking shape at line 1690.
